title: The names tree nuts hide behind
standfirst: Tree nuts goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name tree nuts when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to tree nuts is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to tree-nut is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 13 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act of 2004 (FALCPA), Public Law 108-282, Title II; Sec. 201(qq) FD&C Act (defines 'major food allergen' to include tree nuts)

Guidance for Industry: Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens (Edition 5) / CFSAN tree nut list (almond, beech nut, Brazil nut, butternut, cashew, chestnut, chinquapin, coconut, filbert/hazelnut, ginkgo nut, hickory nut, lichee nut, macadamia/bush nut, pecan, pine/pinon nut, pili nut, pistachio, sheanut, walnut)

Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, Annex II point 8: 'Nuts, namely almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, pecan nuts, Brazil nuts, pistachio nuts, macadamia or Queensland nuts, and products thereof'
EFSA NDA Panel, Scientific Opinion on the evaluation of allergenic foods and food ingredients for labelling purposes, EFSA Journal 12(11):3894
Tree Nut Allergy overview and cross-contact/hidden-source guidance (marzipan, gianduja, nut pastes, nut oils, natural nut extracts)
FASTER Act of 2021 (Public Law 117-11) — codifies major-allergen framework; sesame added as 9th, tree nuts retained as a category

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not tree nuts. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
